flawed_step: 0010–0011: The assertion |W1| > n/2 merely because α > 0 is false. The hypotheses imply only α ≤ 1/2 and hence |W1| ≥ n/2. Although that weaker inequality still suffices here, this is the first unjustified assertion. The fatal inductive error occurs at 0063.
assessment_summary:
0001: Heading only; no mathematical claim.
0002: A contradiction strategy is legitimate.
0003: This is an informal description of the expansion hypothesis, not a precise inference.
0004: Continuation of the informal description; no new claim.
0005: Setting up the k=2 case is legitimate, although the trivial k=1 case is not explicitly addressed.
0006: This is the correct claim needed for k=2.
0007: The negation of the claim in 0006 is assumed correctly.
0008: Choosing a half-sized subset of W1 is legitimate once |W1| ≥ n/2 is known.
0009: The claimed existence of S is true, but the justification continued in 0010–0011 uses an incorrect strict inequality.
0010: Unjustified: α>0 does not imply |W1|>n/2.
0011: The strict inequality is false when α=1/2; only |W1|≥n/2 follows, though that is enough to choose S. The no-edge consequence is valid.
0012: If no W1–W2 edge exists and S⊆W1, then W2 contains no neighbor of S.
0013: N(S)⊆V\W2 and |V\W2|≤αn follow correctly.
0014: The resulting upper bound |N(S)|≤αn is correct.
0015: The expansion hypothesis applies to the half-sized S.
0016: Its lower bound n/2+αn is indeed greater than αn.
0017: Continuation specifying |S|=n/2; correct.
0018: The contradiction proves the k=2 claim.
0019: Fixing an arbitrary k≥3 is legitimate; despite the label, no induction hypothesis is used.
0020: This correctly states the desired layered sequence.
0021: Assuming that no such sequence exists is a valid contradiction setup.
0022: A layered graph can be constructed, with separate layer-copies understood if the Wi overlap.
0023: Directing original graph adjacencies between consecutive layers is valid.
0024: The base case shows that each consecutive pair of layers has at least one connecting edge, but not that every vertex has an outgoing edge; interpreted as a layer-level existence statement, it is correct for i<k.
0025: Searching from all vertices of W1 is legitimate.
0026: This introduces the reachability definitions correctly.
0027: Treating every W1 vertex as a source is correct.
0028: R1:=W1 is therefore correct.
0029: The stated definition of R2 is correct.
0030: R2=N(R1)∩W2 correctly describes the next reachable layer.
0031: These are precisely the vertices reachable by one layered edge.
0032: The analogous definition of R3 is correct.
0033: R3=N(R2)∩W3 is correct.
0034: The reachability interpretation is correct.
0035: Extending the definition to every later layer is legitimate.
0036: The recurrence Ri=N(Ri−1)∩Wi is correct.
0037: The recurrence has the stated reachability interpretation.
0038: If no full layered path exists, then Rk=∅; correct.
0039: A least empty layer exists under that assumption.
0040: R1 is nonempty because feasibility of the expansion bound gives α≤1/2 and hence |W1|≥n/2>0; thus 2≤m≤k.
0041: Minimality of m implies all earlier Ri are nonempty.
0042: Page-number artifact; no mathematical claim.
0043: Blank formatting line; no mathematical claim.
0044: Rm=∅ by definition of m.
0045: Every vertex of Rm−1 has no neighbor in Wm because Rm=N(Rm−1)∩Wm is empty.
0046: Any such neighbor would indeed belong to Rm.
0047: This correctly completes the contradiction establishing 0045.
0048: Rm−1⊆Wm−1 follows from its definition.
0049: Unjustified: enlarging Rm−1 inside Wm−1 need not preserve the property of having no neighbors in Wm.
0050: Consequently, the promised construction of a violating half-set has not been established.
0051: The case |Rm−1|≥n/2 is a legitimate case split.
0052: If |Rm−1|>n/2, S cannot equal all of Rm−1 while having size n/2; choosing a half-sized subset is the valid option.
0053: A half-sized subset of Rm−1 exists in this case and inherits its lack of neighbors in Wm.
0054: The complementary case |Rm−1|<n/2 is correctly identified.
0055: Continuation of the displayed inequality; no new inference.
0056: Rm−1 can be extended to a half-sized subset of Wm−1 because |Wm−1|≥n/2.
0057: The stated strict inequality |Wm−1|>n/2 need not hold when α=1/2, although the required extension still follows from ≥n/2.
0058: Choosing the extension to have size n/2 is possible.
0059: Continuation of the size condition; correct.
0060: Rm−1⊆S⊆Wm−1 is correct, but S⊆Wm−1 does not imply S∩Wm=∅ because the Wi may overlap.
0061: In either branch one can obtain S⊆Wm−1 of size n/2.
0062: The assertion that this S has no neighbor in Wm is not established in the small-|Rm−1| branch.
0063: Invalid: from Rm−1⊆S and the fact that Rm−1 has no edges to Wm, it does not follow that the additional vertices of S have no edges to Wm.
0064: The conclusion N(S)⊆V\Wm therefore does not follow in the small-set branch.
0065: This inclusion is unsupported for the constructed S.
0066: Transitional line only.
0067: The numerical bound would follow from 0065, but 0065 has not been proved.
0068: The expansion hypothesis would apply if a suitable half-sized S had been established.
0069: The lower bound is indeed greater than αn.
0070: Continuation specifying the half-size condition; correct.
0071: The claimed contradiction is unavailable because the needed upper bound on N(S) is unsupported.
0072: The proof has not validly contradicted the assumption of no layered path.
0073: Therefore the conclusion that a full layered path exists is not established by this argument.
0074: Conditional on Rk being nonempty, following predecessor edges would produce vertices vi∈Wi.
0075: Those predecessor edges would give all required consecutive adjacencies.
0076: This would be the desired constrained sequence, but its existence was not proved because of the gap at 0063.
